Memory Architectures Papers

CALMem, CPP, Context Recycling, Rag.NET, OpenAI Sessions - Dual memory, segmented episodic memory, bounded hierarchical context

## Paper Summaries ### CALMem: Dual Memory for Conversational AI | Field | Detail | |-------|--------| | **Title** | Application-Layer Dual Memory for Conversational AI: Achieving Virtually Unbounded Context Without Model Modification | | **Venue** | arXiv:2605.20724 (2026) | | **Key Innovation** | Dual memory: Episodic (sliding-window vector embeddings) + Semantic (agent-writable structured facts) | **Architecture**: ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐ │ CALMem Architecture │ ├─────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Episodic Memory (Vector Store) │ │ - Sliding window embeddings │ │ - Intra-session retrieval │ ├─────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Semantic Memory (Structured Facts) │ │ - Agent-writable facts │ │ - Cross-session persistence │ ├─────────────────────────────────────┤ │ MOIM Injector │ │ - Token-budget adaptive injection │ │ - Prepends relevant context │ └─────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` **Key Innovations**: - **Episodic Memory**: Vector embeddings of conversation turns, sliding window - **Semantic Memory**: Agent-writable structured facts (explicit knowledge) - **MOIM (Message of Injected Memory)**: Auto-retrieves relevant context, scales with budget - **Intra-session retrieval**: Recalls compacted-away turns from CURRENT session (novel!) **Results**: ~750 tokens/turn injected vs 22K baseline; 1-2 orders magnitude cost reduction --- ### CPP: Context Persistence Protocol | Field | Detail | |-------|--------| | **Title** | Bounded Conversational Memory with Hybrid Retrieval and Evidence Highlighting | | **Venue** | SIGDIAL 2026 | | **Key Innovation** | Context Persistence Protocol (CPP) — segmented episodic memory | **Four Phases**: 1. **Segmentation**: 3-10 turns/segment, cosine δ boundary 2. **Dual-Indexing**: Lexical (BM25) + Semantic (embedding) per segment 3. **Budgeted Retrieval**: Top segments under hard storage budget 4. **Evidence Highlighting**: Single most informative sentence per segment **Segmentation**: Cosine similarity drop below δ between turns → new segment **Results**: Matches unbounded baseline on LoCoMo; better on multi-hop; marginal deficit on open-domain --- ### Context Recycling: Hierarchical Memory | Field | Detail | |-------|--------| | **Title** | Context Recycling for Long-Horizon LLM Inference | | **Venue** | arXiv:2606.26105 (2026) | | **Key Innovation** | Hierarchical layers: L0 (500) + L1 (2-10K) + L2 (~1K) | **Three Layers**: - **L0 Permanent** (500 tokens): System prompt, core facts - **L1 Loaded Branch** (2-10K): Active knowledge per turn - **L2 Compacted History** (~1K): Compressed session history **Results**: | Turn | Baseline | Context Recycling | |------|----------|-------------------| | 1 | ~500 | ~850 | | 50 | ~22,000 | ~850 | | 1K | ~200,000 | ~850 | --- ### Rag.NET: Composable Memory Layers | Field | Detail | |-------|--------| | **Source** | GitHub: MarcelRoozekrans/Rag.NET | | **Key Innovation** | Two composable layers: In-session + Cross-session | **Layer 1 - ConversationMemoryPipeline (In-session)**: - Sliding window (MaxExchanges) - Token budget (MaxTokens) - Optional LLM summary (UseSummary) **Layer 2 - PersistentConversationMemory**: - Embeds each exchange → vector store - Keyed by sessionId - Injects relevant past exchanges as system prefix --- ### OpenAI Session Memory | Field | Detail | |-------|--------| | **Source** | OpenAI Cookbook / Responses API | | **Implementations** | TrimmingSession, SummarizingSession | --- ## Comparison Table | System | Segmentation | Retrieval | Budget | Cross-Session | Novelty | |--------|--------------|-----------|--------|---------------|---------| | **CPP** | Cosine δ (3-10 turns) | Hybrid (lexical + semantic) | Hard budget | Yes (segments) | Segment evidence highlighting | | **CALMem** | Sliding window + facts | Episodic + Semantic | Token-budget adaptive | Yes (semantic layer) | Dual memory + MOIM | | **Context Recycling** | Hierarchical (L0/L1/L2) | Layer-based | Fixed budget | Yes (hierarchical) | Bounded context (850 tok) | | **Rag.NET** | Sliding window + summary | Vector store | MaxExchanges/MaxTokens | Yes (vector store) | Composable layers | | **OpenAI** | Trimming / Summarizing | Built-in | Max turns / summary | Yes (session object) | Built-in API | --- ## Our Implementation vs Papers | Aspect | Our Fix (T4+T8) | CPP | CALMem | Context Recycling | |--------|----------------|-----|--------|-------------------| | **Segmentation** | Implicit (generic turn count) | Cosine δ threshold | Sliding window | Hierarchical L0/L1/L2 | | **Sticky Carry** | Filter_path injection | Segment retrieval | Episodic recall | L1 branch loading | | **Decay** | After 3 generic turns | Segment boundary | Sliding window | L2 compaction | | **Budget** | Implicit (filter_path) | Hard storage budget | Token-budget adaptive | Fixed 850 tok/turn | | **Cross-Session** | No (single session) | Yes (segment store) | Yes (semantic layer) | Yes (hierarchical) | --- ## Architecture: Our Sticky Flow vs Papers ```mermaid flowchart TD A[User Query] --> B[Load Checkpoint] B --> C{Sticky Applied?} C -->|Yes| D[Count Generic Turns
(our T8: simple count)] D --> E{> decay_threshold?} E -->|Yes| F[Decay: sticky=None
(CPP: segment boundary)] E -->|No| G[Inject filter_path
(CALMem: episodic recall)] C -->|No| H[Normal Classify/Infer] F --> H G --> I[Retrieve with filter_path] H --> I I --> J[Generate] J --> K[Save Checkpoint] ``` --- ## Future: Toward CALMem/CPP | Enhancement | Based On | Effort | |-------------|----------|--------| | Cosine-based segmentation | CPP | Medium | | Semantic fact layer | CALMem | High | | Hierarchical context (L0/L1/L2) | Context Recycling | High | | Cross-session vector recall | Rag.NET / CALMem | Medium | | Evidence highlighting per segment | CPP | Low | --- ## Related Pages - [Problem: Sticky Context Decay](../problems/sticky-context.html) - [Paper: Subspace Filtering](./subspace-filtering.html) - [Paper: Retrieval Fusion & RRF](./retrieval-fusion.html) - [Architecture: CPP/CALMem](../architectures.html#cpp-calmem)
